THE EARTH

Shape of Earth

  • Shape of Earth is Geoid or Oblate Spheroid (a little flat from top and bottom) and bulged at the center.
  • Reason: Centrifugal force (due to rotation of Earth).
Radius of EarthCircumference of Earth
Equatorial radius: 6378 kmPolar: 40,007.863 km
Polar radius: 6357 kmEquatorial: 40,075 km
Mean radius: 6371Mean: 40,040 km
  • Equatorial speed > Polar speed.
  • Equatorial radii > Polar radii.
  • Equatorial circumference > Polar circumference. (All because the Earth is bulged at the equator and flattened at the poles)

Rotation of Earth

  • Earth rotates on its own axis, from West to East (Anticlockwise).
  • One rotation of Earth = 23 hours 56 minutes 4 seconds.
  • Rotational speed is maximum at the equator and minimum at the poles.
  • Day and night are caused by the Earth's rotation on its axis.

Revolution of Earth

  • Earth revolves around the Sun in elliptical orbit.
  • One revolution = 365 days 6 hours 9 minutes and 9 seconds.
  • Orbital speed = 29.8 km/sec.
  • Mercury has the maximum orbital speed.
  • Neptune has the minimum orbital speed.
  • The Earth's revolution around the sun and the tilt of its axis cause the seasons.

Distance of Earth from Sun and Moon

SunMoon
The point in a planet's orbit when it is closest to the Sun is called Perihelion. On January 3rd, the Earth is nearest to the Sun (147 million km).The point in the moon's orbit when it is closest to Earth is called Perigee. At perigee, the moon appears larger in the sky.
The point in a planet's orbit when it is farthest from the Sun is called Aphelion. On July 4th, the Earth is farthest from Sun (152 million km).The point in the moon's orbit when it is farthest from Earth is called Apogee. At apogee, the moon's tide-raising force is smaller, and the tidal ranges are less than average.

Inclination of Earth's Axis

  • Axial inclination: Inclination of Earth on its axis = 23½°
  • Orbital inclination: Inclination of Earth on its orbital plane = 66½°

LATITUDE AND LONGITUDE

Latitude

  • They are imaginary horizontal lines on the globe that run from East to West.
  • It is the angular distance of a place from the equator.
  • Total latitude = 181.
  • Distance between each latitude is same.
  • 1° of latitude = 111 km.

#### Important Latitudes

  • 0°: Equator (divides Earth into two equal parts) → Northern and Southern Hemisphere.
  • 23½°N: Tropic of Cancer.
  • 66½°N: Arctic Circle.
  • 23½°S: Tropic of Capricorn.
  • 66½°S: Antarctic Circle.
  • Largest latitude: Equator.
  • Smallest latitude: Poles (North and South).
All parallel circles from the equator to the poles are known as "Parallels of Latitude".

#### Uses of Latitude

  1. 1. Climatology
  • Temperature zones and wind
  • Pressure system
  • Planetary wind system
  1. 2. Location of place

Longitude

  • They are imaginary vertical lines over the globe that run North to South.
  • Distance between each longitude decreases from Equator towards poles, at the poles it is 0, while it is maximum at the equator (111.32 km).
  • Total longitudes = 360.

#### Important Meridians (Longitudes)

  • Prime Meridian = 0° longitude (passes through Greenwich, London).
  • International Date Line = 180° Meridian.
  • Prime Meridian also known as International Meridian or Greenwich Meridian. It passes through:
CountryCodeCountryCode
Burkina FasoBGhanaG
SpainSAlgeriaA
FranceFMali → In TOGOMe
UK
TRICK TO REMEMBER: BSF Game in TOGO KINGDOM

#### Concept of Time using Longitude

  • 360° = 24 hours
  • 360° / 24 = 1 hour → Distance rotated by Earth in 1 hour
  • 15° = 1 hour
  • 1° = 60/15 = 4 minutes → Time taken in each 1°
  • Moving East away from Prime Meridian, the time will increase by an hour for every 15°, consecutively if we move to West from the Prime Meridian, the time will decrease by an hour for every 15°.
  • Entire earth is divided into 24 Times Zones. France has the most number of Time Zones (13), Russia (11 time zones), US (6 time zones).

#### International Date Line (180° E/W)

  • It is the imaginary zig-zag line passing through the Pacific Ocean from where the date changes.
  • While crossing International Date Line eastbound i.e. from East to West (eg: Japan to USA) → Date is subtracted by 1 or in other words, the person gains a day and vice versa.
Isochrones: They are lines joining points located at equal travel time from a common centre.

Concept of Great Circle

  • A great circle is the largest possible circle that can be drawn around a sphere.
  • It divides the Earth into two equal parts called Hemispheres (Northern and Southern).
  • All longitudes are considered great circles, but only one latitude is considered a great circle and that is Equator (0° latitude).

Hemisphere

  • Equal division of Earth in two parts.
  • Equator: It divides the globe horizontally into two equal parts: Northern and Southern hemisphere.
  • Prime Meridian: It divides the globe vertically in two equal parts: Eastern and Western Hemisphere.

SOLSTICE AND EQUINOX

  • Solstice: A solstice is an astronomical event that occurs twice a year when the sun reaches its highest or lowest point in the sky, resulting in the longest day or shortest day of the year.
Summer SolsticeWinter Solstice
It occurs on 21st JuneIt occurs on 22nd December
It is the longest day of the year in Northern HemisphereIt is the shortest day and longest night of the year in Northern Hemisphere
The vertical rays of Sun are directly overhead on Tropic of CancerThe vertical rays of Sun are directly overhead on Tropic of Capricorn
Northern Hemisphere gets more heatSouthern Hemisphere gets more heat
Continuous sun rays fall on the North Pole for 6 monthsContinuous sun rays fall on the South Pole for 6 months
  • Equinox: An equinox is a time when the Sun's apparent path in the sky crosses the equator, making day and night approximately equal in length. At this position, neither of the pole is tilted towards the Sun.
  • Vernal or Spring equinox: 21st March.
  • Autumnal or Fall equinox: 23rd September.

ECLIPSES

Solar Eclipse

  • Solar Eclipse: It occurs when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun, casting a shadow on Earth. This can only happen during a new moon (Amavasya).

Lunar Eclipse

  • Lunar Eclipse: It occurs when the Earth passes between the Moon and the Sun, casting a shadow on Moon. This can only happen during a full moon (Purnima).

Supermoon

  • A supermoon occurs when the Moon's orbit is closest to the Earth during a full/new moon.
  • The moon appears bigger than its normal size.
When the Sun, Moon and Earth, all are aligned in a straight line, the alignment is known as Syzygy.

TIDES

  • Tides: Tides are the periodic rise and fall of the ocean's water levels. They are caused by the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun on the Earth's oceans. They are of two types:

Neap Tides

  • They occur when Earth, Moon, and Sun are in perpendicular alignment.

Spring Tides

  • They occur when the Earth, Moon, and Sun are all aligned along a straight line.

Flood Tide and Ebb Tide

  • The change from low to high tide is called the "flood tide" or "flow". The change from high to low tide is called "ebb tide".

Torrid, Temperate, and Frigid Zone

  • Torrid Zone: Receives direct overhead rays of the Sun due to which it is the hottest zone. It is located between Tropics.
  • Temperature Zone: Region between Tropic of Cancer & Arctic Circle or Tropic of Capricorn & Antarctic Circle. It receives slanting rays of the Sun.
  • Frigid Zone: Coldest region on Earth which experiences daylight for 6 months and 6 months of night (due to the tilt of Earth). Located beyond Arctic (66½° N) & Antarctic Circle (66½° S).

Key concepts

  • Shape of Earth: Geoid / Oblate Spheroid — bulged at equator, flat at poles (centrifugal force).
  • Radius: Equatorial 6378 km, Polar 6357 km, Mean 6371 km; Circumference: Polar 40,007.863 km, Equatorial 40,075 km, Mean 40,040 km; Equatorial speed > Polar speed.
  • Rotation: West → East (anticlockwise), 23 h 56 min 4 s; rotational speed max at equator, min at poles; causes day and night.
  • Revolution: 365 d 6 h 9 min 9 s in elliptical orbit, 29.8 km/sec; Mercury max orbital speed, Neptune min; revolution + axial tilt cause seasons.
  • Perihelion (closest to Sun, ~3 Jan, 147 M km) vs Aphelion (farthest, ~4 Jul, 152 M km); Perigee (moon closest to Earth) vs Apogee (moon farthest, smaller tidal range).
  • Axial inclination = 23½°; Orbital inclination = 66½°.
  • Latitude — horizontal lines, East-West, angular distance from equator, total 181, 1° = 111 km, all parallel circles = "Parallels of Latitude"; largest = Equator, smallest = Poles.
  • Important latitudes: 0° Equator; 23½°N Tropic of Cancer; 66½°N Arctic Circle; 23½°S Tropic of Capricorn; 66½°S Antarctic Circle.
  • Uses of latitude: Climatology (temperature zones/wind, pressure, planetary wind) + location of place.
  • Longitude — vertical lines, North-South; distance decreases from equator (max 111.32 km) to poles (0); total 360.
  • Prime Meridian (0°, Greenwich, London) = International/Greenwich Meridian; passes through Burkina Faso, Spain, France, Ghana, Algeria, Mali, Togo (TOGO), UK — "BSF Game in TOGO KINGDOM".
  • International Date Line = 180° meridian (zig-zag, Pacific Ocean); crossing East to West (e.g. Japan → USA) subtracts 1 day (gain a day).
  • Time: 360° = 24 h; 15° = 1 h; 1° = 4 min; 24 Time Zones; France = 13 (most), Russia = 11, US = 6.
  • Isochrones — lines joining points at equal travel time from a common centre.
  • Great circle — largest circle on a sphere; divides Earth into two equal hemispheres; all longitudes are great circles; only latitude that is a great circle = Equator.
  • Hemisphere — Equator → Northern/Southern (horizontal); Prime Meridian → Eastern/Western (vertical).
  • Solstice — twice a year; longest/shortest day. Summer Solstice = 21 June (NH longest day, vertical rays on Tropic of Cancer, NH more heat, 6-month sun on North Pole). Winter Solstice = 22 December (NH shortest day, vertical rays on Tropic of Capricorn, SH more heat, 6-month sun on South Pole).
  • Equinox — Sun's apparent path crosses equator; day ≈ night; no pole tilted toward Sun. Vernal/Spring = 21 March; Autumnal/Fall = 23 September.
  • Solar Eclipse — Moon between Earth and Sun, on new moon (Amavasya). Types: Partial, Annular, Total.
  • Lunar Eclipse — Earth between Moon and Sun, on full moon (Purnima). Red Moon (Earth refracts light; blue scatters more so red reaches moon) / Blue Moon (two full moons in one calendar month).
  • Supermoon — Moon at perigee during full/new moon, appears bigger.
  • Syzygy — Sun, Moon, Earth aligned in a straight line.
  • Tides — periodic rise/fall of sea levels due to Moon and Sun gravity. Neap Tides = perpendicular alignment (Earth-Moon-Sun). Spring Tides = straight-line alignment. Flood tide/flow = low → high; Ebb tide = high → low; Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat) has max tidal energy potential.
  • Torrid Zone — between Tropics, overhead Sun rays, hottest. Temperate Zone — between Tropic of Cancer & Arctic / Tropic of Capricorn & Antarctic, slanting rays. Frigid Zone — beyond Arctic/Antarctic Circle, coldest, 6 months day + 6 months night.
